subject: Architecture
title: The Woolworth Building: Cathedral of Commerce
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Woolworth Building: Cathedral of Commerce.

hook.text: Frank Woolworth paid $13.5 million in cash for the world's tallest building — no mortgage.

buildup.text: At 792 feet, the Woolworth Building was the tallest in the world from 1913 to 1930.

discovery.text: Architect Cass Gilbert clad a steel frame in Gothic terracotta — a skyscraper dressed as a cathedral.

twist.text: Inside the lobby, a sculpture shows Woolworth counting nickels — he built his empire on five-cent stores.

climax.text: A minister called it the 'Cathedral of Commerce,' and the nickname stuck permanently.

punchline.text: He sold everything for five cents. Then built the tallest thing on Earth.

quiz.question: How did Woolworth pay for the world's tallest building?
options: A consortium of banks provided the financing
He paid $13.5 million in cash with no mortgage
He traded stock in his retail company
